query: Why is learning satisfaction low for certain groups, and which factors drive it?

per_column.name: pedagogy_adaptation_quality
per_column.rationale: Candidate cause of satisfaction: quality of instructional adaptation plausibly drives learner satisfaction directly.

per_column.name: peer_social_interaction_loss
per_column.rationale: Loss of peer/community interaction is a candidate causal factor for reduced satisfaction; a plausible treatment rather than a common cause.

per_column.name: teacher_feedback_and_responsiveness
per_column.rationale: Feedback quality is a candidate driver of satisfaction, treated here as another causal factor.

per_column.name: async_format_benefit
per_column.rationale: Benefit from asynchronous format is a candidate cause of satisfaction, not a common cause of the other factors.

per_column.name: student_engagement_level
per_column.rationale: Engagement is plausibly downstream of pedagogy/feedback and upstream of satisfaction -- it lies on the causal path, so it is a mediator, not a confounder.

per_column.name: subject_remote_format_fit
per_column.rationale: How well a subject fits remote format plausibly affects both how pedagogy is adapted/feedback given (treatment) and satisfaction (outcome), making it a genuine common cause. Subject is in the original table, but 'remote format fit' is a surfaced construct not named in the query.

judge.rationale: The query is broadly a 'which factors drive satisfaction' attribution question. The system supplied several candidate treatments (pedagogy, peer interaction loss, feedback, async benefit), so a treatment is clearly present. However, causal attribution requires confounders -- common causes of BOTH a treatment and the outcome -- that were surfaced from the data. Most added columns are parallel candidate causes, not confounders. student_engagement_level is best read as a mediator (on the causal path), so treating it as a control would be a mistake. Only subject_remote_format_fit plausibly functions as a common cause (fit shapes both how instruction is delivered and satisfaction), and it was surfaced rather than copied from the query. This is a single, weakly-specified confounder, so the technical claim of setting up an unbiased causal estimation is only partially met.
